title: THE FOUR OLDS audio play — a11_baytwo

lines.sfx: In Fabrication Bay Two two hundred workers stand quiet on the concrete, and a PA clicks on over them.
Mira Vess, forties, in a dark suit, steps to the microphone in front of the whole shift.

lines.text: Bay Two closes today. Every one of you is paid twelve months at full rate, and your medical stays on the whole time.

lines.sfx: A woman starts down the rows, and a printed card goes into each man's hand.

lines.text: There's a card coming to you. It puts you first in line if this floor ever runs again.
(then) I don't expect you to believe that means anything. Keep the card anyway.

lines.sfx: A worker near the front steps out of his row, his boots scuffing the concrete.

lines.text: My father cut the first nozzle ring in this bay!
I know he did. His name is on the wall of the visitor center.
(then) The tooling gets declared surplus and sold at public auction. An outside outfit comes in to pallet it up and count it.

lines.sfx: At the back wall Mack Boone, fifty-five, shifts his weight, and a folding chair creaks behind him.

lines.text: Whatever you need to think about today, put it on me.

lines.sfx: Pell, the compliance administrator, steps in at her shoulder with his tablet up.

lines.text: The Monitorship views this as a, a meaningful posture of alignment. I'll be noting the, ah, expedited timeline favorably.

lines.sfx: She walks out, and her heels on the concrete are the only sound in the bay.
Later the bay doors stand open to the lot, and men carry toolboxes and milk crates out toward the fence.
Out at the fence a camera shutter clacks once and a knot of reporters murmurs behind it.
Tito Alvarez, twenty-four, latches his toolbox on the bench and picks up his hood.
Mack stops at the bench and picks up a practice weld, two plates run together in one bead with no start or stop to it, and turns it over.

lines.text: I just got fired, Mr. Boone.
I know what happened. Keep your tools.

lines.sfx: Tito lifts his box off the bench and goes.
Mack takes a small notebook from his shirt pocket, clicks a pen, and writes one line.
